text: {"summary": "About 40 people were burned during a Tony Robbins seminar firewalk in Dallas, while most of the 7,000 attendees walked safely. The article attributes the injuries to physics: coals must burn down to about 1,000°F with an ash layer, and walkers who linger, such as for selfies, get burned."}
{"summary": "This roundup highlights 11 great 2016 films streaming on Netflix, plus one on Hulu, to help viewers end the year at home. Picks range from Disney's live-action "}

{"summary": "Ratan Tata, Tata Group chairman, said he feels lonely and is in pain amid his ongoing dispute with Cyrus Mistry, accusing critics of damaging his and the group's reputation. He spoke at the Tata Chemicals shareholders' meeting, which had been called to remove Nusli Wadia from the board, and thanked shareholders for their support."}

{"summary": "A heavy smartphone user gave up his beloved Samsung Galaxy S7, which he calls the best phone he's used, for an iPhone 6s Plus. The main reason was battery life: the S7 often died by 5 p.m., while the iPhone, despite a smaller battery, lasts much longer thanks to better software optimization."}

{"summary": "Marine biologists worry that the upcoming sequel Finding Dory could spark a surge in demand for blue tang fish as pets, as Finding Nemo did for clownfish. Blue tangs are rarer, don't do well in tanks, and are collected in lightly regulated waters near Indonesia and the Philippines, risking ecosystem damage. Ellen DeGeneres, Dory's voice, says the film's message is that fish belong in the wild."}

{"summary": "CBS has canceled the sitcom \"We Are Men\" after weak ratings, with its premiere drawing 6.4 million viewers. Starting October 14, \"2 Broke Girls\" moves into its 8:30 p.m. slot, and \"Mike and Molly\" returns to the schedule on November 4."}

{"summary": "Fashion designer Charlotte Ronson's New York City home, featured on Domaine Home, is shown to be stylish yet livable rather than extravagant. White walls, eclectic artwork, bright touches like baby blue dining chairs, and fresh flowers create an airy, comfortable space."}

{"summary": "A Bustle-style roundup of 29 standout pieces of writing by women from 2016, chosen for impact and online availability. It covers topics including Hillary Clinton's nomination, Black Lives Matter, abortion, domestic violence, rape culture, and Donald Trump's election. The list aims to encourage readers to support quality journalism by women."}

{"summary": "ScHoolboy Q revealed he almost quit rap after his sophomore album Oxymoron, taking long breaks that cost him about three years with his daughter. He said he wants to prioritize his family over his career, and fans are now bracing for a possible future departure from music."}

{"summary": "Cinematographer Dean Cundey revealed on a new Scream Factory Blu-ray commentary that he and John Carpenter added a subtle \"eye light\" gleam to human characters in The Thing, letting viewers tell who is still human and who is the shape-shifting monster. The Blu-ray releases October 11th."}

{"summary": "The nation's food industry has announced plans to simplify food labels with easier-to-understand language, and the changes will soon appear on grocery store shelves. The move aims to reduce consumer confusion about what products contain."}

{"summary": "A BuzzFeed-style roundup of 19 teens who made headlines in 2016 for quirky and viral moments, including a Mulan-themed school ID, a deer named Money as a best friend, a teen stuck in a Barney costume for 45 minutes, and a girl who found a dead body while playing Pokemon Go."}

{"summary": "The Commerce Commission's 2016 Consumer Issues Paper names Spark (140 complaints) and Vodafone (133) as the most complained-about companies, with pricing the top issue. Both telcos called the results disappointing, while the Commission stressed complaints do not necessarily mean a law was broken."}

{"summary": "Bret and Zach Winingar, riding near Little Rock, Arkansas, found an emaciated, chewed-up dog locked in an animal crate. They rescued her, named her Charlie Bravo (CB), and took her to a vet, where she was estimated to be eight months old. After her story went viral, donations covered her care and funded a new charity called C.B's Angels."}

{"summary": "Amy Cazin, a former stay-at-home mom, started Primal Pit Paste with $100 after seeking safer deodorant for her family. She turned down an early Wal-Mart offer because her company wasn't ready to scale, and her products now sell at Whole Foods."}

{"summary": "Some men are using period-tracking apps such as iAmAMan and uPMS to monitor female colleagues' and partners' menstrual cycles, aiming to avoid moodiness linked to PMS. One woman said her coworkers started tracking her cycle after a workplace argument, and the trend drew widespread public outrage on Twitter."}

{"summary": "An Arkansas man's Roomba spread dog poop across his house after running a scheduled cleaning while he slept. The article uses this incident to argue that home robots and smart appliances, like iRobot's Roomba and Nest thermostats, struggle to add real value in chaotic home environments, which is why they remain niche products."}

{"summary": "McLaren plans to spend £1 billion over six years on research and development for 15 new cars by 2022, including a P1 successor. The investment focuses on new powertrains, hybrid drivetrains, carbon fiber structures, and an all-electric model, aiming to grow annual sales from 2,000 to 5,000 supercars."}

{"summary": "Amateur archaeologists from Underground Rome have uncovered a previously unmapped passageway beneath Hadrian's Villa in Tivoli, Italy. The tunnels, likely used by slaves and merchants to run the estate unseen, connect the Academy area to a 2.5-mile underground roadway. Researchers say the passage may have served as a private retreat for the emperor."}

{"summary": "Health experts Melisse Gelula and Alexia Brue explain why bone broth, a slow-cooked soup made from animal bones, is worth adding to your diet. They cite benefits such as calcium, magnesium, and collagen, and say it can be a filling morning drink. The article also includes a bone broth recipe."}

{"summary": "This satirical article, labeled as fiction, pokes fun at rumored details about GTA VI, including its release delays, main characters, improved graphics, online server problems, and microtransactions. It is not a real announcement from Rockstar Games."}

{"summary": "Whole Foods co-CEO Walter Robb says he never hires people who lack humility or show an excess of self-promotion. Google shares that value, seeking people who accept better ideas, while experts advise candidates to promote their value to the organization rather than themselves."}

{"summary": "The article explains why Indian ceiling fans usually have three blades while US fans often have four. US fans, which mainly supplement air conditioning, use four blades to move a large mass of air slowly, whereas Indian fans are lighter, run faster, and are energy efficient stand-alone cooling appliances."}

{"summary": "This Guardian-style roundup lists 20 smartphone apps that encourage people to get outdoors, covering activities such as hiking, geocaching, stargazing, dog-friendly beach visits, fishing, camping and parkour. Highlights include Forest XPlorer, ViewRanger, the Gruffalo Spotter and Star Walk 2."}

{"summary": "An article claims that The Biggest Loser, a long-running NBC weight-loss show, produced only temporary results for its contestants, who lost weight through intense daily training while on the program. It frames the show's transformations as a misleading success story."}

{"summary": "Harvard psychiatrist Robert Waldinger, who leads the 75-year Grant Study tracking men's lives, concludes that close, stable relationships are the key to happiness and health. Isolation predicts earlier health decline and shorter lives, while wealth, fame, and career success do not bring the same benefits."}

{"summary": "Jessica Simpson wore an all-black outfit with skinny jeans and stilettos for a Mexican dinner in Calabasas with fiance Eric Johnson and their daughter Maxwell. Three months after giving birth to son Ace, she says she is done having children, but hinted at returning to the studio to make music."}

{"summary": "In September 2015, Leann surprised her grandfather Ried with the news that she was expecting twins, hiding the fact until the reveal. His emotional reaction to the first ultrasound, including tears and a swear word, was captured on video. Leann later gave birth to twin girls in February 2016."}

{"summary": "The article lists 15 lesser-known facts about Tesla cars, including Easter eggs like Rainbow Road and a James Bond submersible mode, plans for a semitruck and driverless bus, and the Model S's record-breaking safety rating and 315-mile range. It also covers Musk's SEXY naming idea and the Model 3 name change."}

{"summary": "The Battlefield 1 Open Beta will end on Thursday, September 8, and EA has patched the Sinai Desert Conquest mode to remove time limits so games run until one team reaches 250 points. EA also plans server stress tests that may cause downtime, and the full game launches October 21."}

{"summary": "With the U.S. lifting its arms embargo on Vietnam, the article examines who buys the most American weapons. Saudi Arabia and the UAE top the list, followed by Turkey, South Korea, Australia, and others, with the Middle East accounting for about 40% of U.S. arms exports."}

{"summary": "Nine-year-old Molly Sings performed Kasey Chambers' song 'Am I Not Pretty Enough?' in her blind audition on The Voice Kids Australia, moving the judges to tears. Mel B. then praised her confidence and chose her, saying 'Girl Power!' and urging her to join her team."}

{"summary": "Sen. Elizabeth Warren insists she is not running for president, but her new memoir, A Fighting Chance, makes a strong case for a bid. The book recounts her reluctant public moves, such as the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and her Senate run, and her repeated calls to fight for the middle class."}

{"summary": "BBC golf commentator Peter Alliss was caught on a hot mic at the Masters calling Sergio Garcia's fiancée Angela Akins's skirt 'the shortest skirt in the country' and joking about their night ahead. The BBC apologized, and the 86-year-old has faced criticism for past sexist and racist remarks."}

{"summary": "All 391 apartments offered by LendLease at Darling Square in Sydney sold out within four hours on Saturday, drawing more than 400 buyers and signaling strong demand for inner-city homes despite looming oversupply. The sellout comes as investor confidence rebounds and interest rates fall, even though tens of thousands of new apartments are due for completion."}

{"summary": "Lindsay Lohan posted an Instagram photo of herself in a recording studio with Duran Duran's Simon le Bon and Nick Rhodes, alongside her younger sister, singer Ali Lohan. The post comes after Lohan's recent West End stage run and the end of her probation for a 2011 necklace theft."}

{"summary": "Bill Maher warned TV hosts interviewing President-elect Donald Trump to hold him accountable and not let him use their shows, citing Jimmy Fallon's September interview as an example. Maher said he would still welcome Trump on his HBO show, noting Trump's unpredictability."}

{"summary": "The article predicts that the traditional 9-5 workday will fade within 15 years as millennials, who value flexible schedules, work-family balance, and continuing education, enter the workforce. It cites cheaper, less essential offices, remote-work productivity gains, and growing trust in these practices as drivers of the shift."}

{"summary": "The tiny plastic tripod in pizza boxes is called a pizza saver, invented by Long Island woman Carmela Vitale, who patented the design in 1985 to keep sagging box lids from ripping cheese off pizzas. Though inexpensive, it has generated significant profits for manufacturers, while Vitale never profited from it herself."}

{"summary": "A ranked list of the ten worst sports seasons in New York history, from the 1972-73 Islanders to the 1983-88 Columbia football team, which holds the No. 1 spot with its 44-game losing streak. The 2014-15 Knicks, at 5-36, rank second."}

{"summary": "Researchers Yonat Zwebner and colleagues ran experiments finding that people shown a headshot and several possible names can pick the correct name more often than chance, suggesting people come to resemble their names. The study involved institutions in Israel and France."}

{"summary": "A study of former Biggest Loser contestants found their metabolisms stayed slowed, making weight regain nearly inevitable, and host Bob Harper suggested intermittent fasting, such as skipping breakfast, to help maintain losses. Experts say evidence on long-term effectiveness is lacking."}

{"summary": "Drake's album \"Views\" has topped the Billboard 200 for nine straight weeks, the longest consecutive run since Adele's \"21\" in 2012. Unlike earlier blockbusters, its recent chart success relies mostly on streaming, with about 77% of its latest sales coming from streams. A tenth week at No. 1 would tie Adele's record."}

{"summary": "Glee star Alex Newell has joined the cast of Geography Club, a film adaptation of Brent Hartinger's popular novel. Newell, who plays transgender character Unique on Glee, said the script appealed to him because it could open more people's eyes to transgender experiences. He joins Scott Bakula, Ana Gasteyer, and other young stars in the cast."}

{"summary": "A listicle compiles anonymous former fast food and restaurant employees' warnings about menu items to avoid, including reheated popcorn at movie theaters, reused chicken nuggets at McDonald's, water-soaked hot dogs at ballparks, and stale chicken in KFC's BBQ sandwich. Panera's fresh sandwiches and salads are recommended instead."}

{"summary": "A reader told Jezebel that Galbani's reduced-fat string cheese packaging features a female cartoon character, while all full-fat versions show male characters. The reader's young daughter noticed the difference and asked for the 'girl cheese.' A photo and Galbani's website images appear to confirm the pattern."}

{"summary": "A 1964 photo shows Alfred Hitchcock wearing a Beatles-style mop-top wig, humorously resembling Stooge Moe Howard. Retronaut shared the image, and the reason for the disguise remains unexplained."}

{"summary": "A Bangalore Mirror reporter searched Tamil Nadu's forests for the Irula tribe's famed rat catchers, whose skills drew attention after two Irula men were flown to Florida to hunt Burmese pythons. The trip ends at a remote hilltop, where 60-year-old Eranna, the last known rat catcher in hundreds of villages, explains his traditional methods and why his skill is fading."}

{"summary": "Bill Carter, a New York Times TV reporter for over 25 years and author of The Late Shift, is taking a voluntary buyout amid the paper's push to get 100 employees to leave. He calls the decision agonizing but says the severance is too good to pass up, and he is looking for a new job and working on a late-night TV book."}

{"summary": "Google quietly created a limited liability company, Google Auto LLC, in 2011 to legally operate its self-driving car project. The LLC is listed as manufacturer of all 23 of Google's Lexus self-driving cars, likely to shield Google's assets from trouble, and Google plans to seek established automakers as manufacturing partners."}

{"summary": "A couple from Gujarat's tribal Dahod district has finally undergone a family planning operation after having 17 children, 16 daughters and one son. Villagers urged them to stop, as the husband kept trying for another son and the family struggled to feed everyone amid inflation."}

{"summary": "An opinion piece defends multi-level marketing businesses, often promoted on social media by mothers, arguing they are legitimate small businesses rather than illegal pyramid schemes. The author says these entrepreneurs offer financial freedom amid economic pressures and urges readers to consider supporting them."}

{"summary": "Orphan Black's Comic-Con panel featured a blooper reel released by BBC America, after the fourth season ended. One clip shows Tatiana Maslany, as Cosima, repeatedly fumbling a line on the phone, a mistake the article suggests she frequently makes."}

{"summary": "Bloomberg uses alternative food indexes, including lattes, pizza, Hooters wings, and Nobu black cod, to gauge currency values beyond the Big Mac. The strong dollar appears overvalued against the yen and pound in several comparisons, while London is notably expensive and the euro looks undervalued based on Frankfurt pizza prices."}

{"summary": "Repeated studies, including a large 2012 Canadian study of over 200,000 people, found fasting has little effect on cholesterol test results, though it may give a clearer picture of triglycerides. Many European countries no longer require fasting, and experts say dropping the requirement would make testing easier for patients."}

{"summary": "In Hoedspruit, South Africa, rock-throwing children forced a genet mother to abandon her babies. The orphanage's founders hand-fed the newborns, but a poodle-cocker spaniel mix named Candy, who unexpectedly produced milk, nursed them. Two genets were later released into the wild, while Chouchou stayed at the center."}

{"summary": "The article examines a viral 1995 video of a Mike Tyson fight that some believe shows a time traveler holding a cameraphone. Snopes notes the device was likely a handheld camera widely available in 1995, such as the Casio QV-10A. The piece argues that people often misread old footage through modern assumptions, like a 1922 \"wireless phone\" that was really a radio."}

{"summary": "California-based Turing Robotic Industries has unveiled the Turing Phone Cadenza, a concept smartphone running its Swordfish OS with deep learning AI. Its listed specs include 12GB RAM, 1TB internal storage, a 60MP rear camera, a 5.8-inch Quad HD display, and support for four SIM cards. It is expected to release next year."}

{"summary": "Michigan mom Dayna Mager, 28, says she responds every time her baby daughter Luella cries, rather than letting her cry it out. Her approach was inspired by a missionary's account of silent, untended babies in a Ugandan orphanage. Her photo of sleeping in the crib with Luella went viral on Facebook."}

{"summary": "GrubHub analyzed ordering at more than 350 college campuses and found Syracuse University students order the most late-night food, with 1 in 4 orders placed between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m. Overall, college students are 87 percent more likely than average diners to order late-night meals, and 28 percent less likely to choose healthier options."}

{"summary": "A lighthearted guide to staying healthy in 2017 with minimal effort, skipping the gym entirely. Tips include cutting back on sugary juice, sitting with good posture, breathing correctly, gardening, moving for 10 minutes daily, taking park walks, sneezing freely, limiting Twitter, and drinking a glass of warm water."}

{"summary": "M&M's is releasing M&M's Mega in May 2014, an original and peanut version packed with three times the chocolate of regular M&M's. Small bags cost $1.49 and medium bags $3.29, following focus group requests for bigger candies."}

{"summary": "A Lovehoney survey of 4,400 of its customers found sex lasts an average of 19 minutes, including about ten minutes of foreplay. Just over half were happy with that, though 19% of women and 23% of men wished it lasted longer, and many wanted more than 15 minutes or over half an hour."}

{"summary": "Nintendo's $60 NES Classic Edition, releasing this November with 30 classic games, cannot connect to the internet or accept cartridges or other add-ons, so no additional games will ever be released for it. Nintendo says it is a standalone device aimed at casual and nostalgic players rather than hardcore gamers."}

{"summary": "A simple experiment shows that pouring milk into Coca-Cola causes the milk to curdle and separate, with solid chunks settling at the bottom. The reaction is attributed to Coke's phosphoric acid, which researchers suspect may reduce bone density, though more research is needed."}

{"summary": "The USDA approved four Chinese poultry processors to ship cooked chicken meat to the U.S., initially limited to U.S.-raised birds. Critics warn the rules could later allow Chinese-raised poultry, which would not require origin labeling and would lack on-site USDA supervision."}

{"summary": "Actor Alison Pill, of Newsroom, explained on Conan O'Brien's show that she accidentally tweeted a topless photo of herself after a touch-screen mishap with her new BlackBerry. She called the incident dumb and hideously embarrassing, saying she felt awkward meeting people for months afterward. She had deleted the photo and apologized at the time."}

{"summary": "At Wasatch High School in Heber City, Utah, student Ben Schofield's American flag was set on fire in the parking lot, scorching his truck. Classmates extinguished the blaze, and the next day dozens of students rallied in red, white and blue to show they would not be silenced. Police and the school district are investigating."}

{"summary": "A farmer near Buenos Aires, Argentina, discovered a large buried object on Christmas Day that paleontologists identified as the shell of an ancient glyptodon, an armored relative of the armadillo that could weigh up to two tons and lived during the Pleistocene epoch. The fossil is at least 10,000 years old."}

{"summary": "Labrador retrievers remained America's most popular dog breed for a 26th straight year, according to the American Kennel Club's new rankings. Rottweilers rose to No. 8, their highest ranking in almost 20 years, while French bulldogs and other breeds also climbed the popularity list."}

{"summary": "Anthony surprised his 17-year-old sister Anelle at her high school graduation by showing up in a cap and gown. Anelle said she struggled not to laugh onstage, and the prank drew laughs from classmates and families who recognized him."}
{"summary": "Michel Bechard was arrested Friday after he stripped naked at a White House security gate and, according to the Secret Service, assaulted a uniformed officer who tried to subdue him."}

{"summary": "A viral Twitter theory by user @strnks reimagines the ending of 'Friends': instead of the gang leaving their apartment, the show would end with Phoebe, a former meth user, staring through the window at Central Perk. In this version, the entire 10 seasons are her fevered daydream about the friends' lives."}

{"summary": "The article claims that bay leaves are a natural cockroach repellent because roaches dislike their smell and use fecal odors to locate food and water. It advises placing dried, crushed bay leaves in corners, kitchens, and gardens to deter infestations."}

{"summary": "EA Sports' Madden NFL 2016 simulated Super Bowl 50 and predicted the Carolina Panthers will beat the Denver Broncos 24-20, with Cam Newton named MVP. The game has correctly picked the Super Bowl winner nine times in 12 years, though it missed the 2013 Seahawks blowout."}

{"summary": "Mary Lou Bruner, a Texas State Board of Education candidate known for conspiracy theories such as claims about Noah's ark, Obama, and the New World Order, lost her race to chiropractor Kevin M. Ellis by a wide margin. Her controversial Facebook posts overshadowed her other platforms."}

{"summary": "The FBI has arrested a man suspected of contaminating salad bars and prepared foods with a mixture of hand cleaner, water, and Tomcat mice poison at a Whole Foods in Ann Arbor, Michigan, and possibly at a Meijer and other stores in Flint. Whole Foods threw out and replaced the affected food, and no illnesses have been reported. His motive is unknown and he could face felony charges for food adulteration."}

{"summary": "Researchers report in Nature Geoscience that Tamu Massif, a huge underwater volcano beneath the northwest Pacific's Shatsky Rise, is the largest known volcano on Earth, about 400 miles wide. It erupted around 144 million years ago and was previously thought to be part of an oceanic plateau."}

{"summary": "The August 10, 2014 full moon will be the largest supermoon of the year, reaching full at 2:10 p.m. EDT and visible Sunday night after sunset. Supermoons can appear up to 14 percent closer and 30 percent brighter than other full moons, and it may pair with the Perseid meteor shower."}
{"summary": "Simpsons writer John Swartzwelder has joined Twitter, but instead of expert self-promotion he posts only dry, deadpan quotes from his detective novels, like "}

{"summary": "The article explores why cats purr, noting that purring may signal not only happiness but also anxiety, self-healing, hunger, or an appeasing gesture. Scientists link the 25-150 Hz frequency to bone and muscle repair, though the true meaning remains uncertain."}

{"summary": "Actress Shailene Woodley, 22, of the film Divergent, has become known for repeatedly using the word \"badass\" in interviews. A timeline of quotes from 2013 and 2014 shows her applying it to her character Tris, co-star Theo James, author Veronica Roth, and stunts."}

{"summary": "Speedrunner BubblesDelFuego has beaten Fallout 4 in just over an hour by exploiting glitches like quick reload, item climbing, Power Armor clipping, and cover slides, which teleport the character across the map. The community is still developing these techniques and believes the record could drop to 45-55 minutes."}

{"summary": "A roundup of ten under-the-radar pop songs from March, sidestepping chart giants like Drake and Ed Sheeran. Picks include The Drums' \"Blood Under My Belt,\" Offaiah's \"Run,\" Nelly Furtado's \"Phoenix,\" Amine's \"REDMERCEDES,\" and Steps' \"Scared of the Dark,\" with critical commentary on each."}

{"summary": "Adrienne Maloof and Paul Nassif, former Real Housewives stars, released a joint statement announcing they have resolved all outstanding issues in their long, messy divorce. They say their three children remain their top priority and that they will co-parent together."}

{"summary": "Melting Arctic sea ice is making it harder for polar bears to hunt seals, and desperate males are increasingly killing and eating younger bears. A National Geographic video reportedly captured an adult male preying on a cub as its mother fled."}

{"summary": "Siphiwe Baleka, founder of Fitness Trucking, says poor sleep disrupts the hormones that regulate hunger and metabolism, contributing to weight gain, especially for truck drivers who average under five hours nightly. He recommends consistent bedtimes, a sleep tracker, and limiting electronics before bed."}

{"summary": "The small cylinder on a laptop charger cord is a ferrite bead, which filters high-frequency electromagnetic interference. Laptop internals generate radio frequencies that the cable can broadcast or pick up, and the bead suppresses these signals so they don't disrupt WiFi, TV, or other electronics."}

{"summary": "Tesla has released 'Part Deux' of its Master Plan, outlining a ten-year direction that includes expanding its lineup with a compact SUV, a pickup truck, a heavy-duty Semi, and urban transport vehicles, alongside reinvented production methods aimed at sustainability."}

{"summary": "This BuzzFeed list recommends 23 products for antisocial people who want to avoid others, including a scarf to deter chatty folks, a bottle opener for drinking alone, an ostrich pillow, socks, prints of famous recluses, and a plant mug. Most items are sold on Amazon or Etsy."}

{"summary": "A preliminary study of nearly 26,000 men in the JAMA Internal Medicine journal found that Viagra users had roughly double the risk of melanoma, a deadly skin cancer, and current users had an 84 percent higher risk. Researchers say it is too early to change prescriptions but urge further investigation, and it conflicts with a 2011 mouse study suggesting Viagra helped defend against melanoma."}

{"summary": "The article argues that an Apple acquisition of Tesla is unlikely to work because Tim Cook and Elon Musk are very different leaders. Cook is a supply-chain manager rather than a visionary, while Musk is an unconventional entrepreneur who would not accept working under anyone, so a deal would likely require Musk's departure."}

{"summary": "AMC's \"Breaking Bad\" is launching an Emmy campaign for the final eight episodes of Season 5, using suggestive billboards across Los Angeles to urge TV Academy voters. The show won Outstanding Drama Series last year, and its spin-off \"Better Call Saul\" is also mentioned as a possible award contender."}

{"summary": "Qantas plans a nonstop Perth-to-London flight covering about 9,008 miles in roughly 17 hours, launching March 2018 as the third-longest flight by distance. The article ranks current long routes, including Air India's Pacific route, and notes Singapore Airlines' planned 10,252-mile New York flight could reshuffle the list."}

{"summary": "Pokemon CEO Tsunekazu Ishihara confirmed Pokemon will support Nintendo's upcoming NX, saying it aims to blur the line between home and handheld consoles. Patents and sources suggest an oval, touchscreen, portable device with detachable controllers, though Nintendo has not officially confirmed details."}

{"summary": "Houston is projected to surpass Chicago as the third-largest US city within eight to 10 years, driven by energy-fueled growth, low taxes, and job opportunities. The city is also becoming more diverse and socially progressive, though it faces air quality and traffic problems, and its energy-dependent economy has been hurt by low oil prices."}

{"summary": "Defence Minister Manohar Parrikar reportedly proposed all-women battalions for combat roles across the Army, Navy and Air Force, citing the induction of women fighter pilots. He said changes should come gradually and urged opening the National Defence Academy and Sainik schools to women. The article, an opinion piece, praises the move as a step toward women's empowerment and recalls Subhas Chandra Bose's Rani of Jhansi Regiment."}

{"summary": "Netflix announced that Orange Is The New Black Season 2 will premiere June 6, during the credits of House of Cards Season 2's finale. Laura Prepon returns as Alex for at least four episodes, and Lori Petty joins the cast."}

{"summary": "The Warriors remain No. 1 in this week's NBA Power Rankings for a fourth straight week after winning nine in a row, but the writer argues the Grizzlies deserve to be considered co-leaders. Memphis has the league's best record at 15 wins, tied for fewest losses, strong defense, and a perfect record against Western Conference foes. The Sixers, as usual, sit at No. 30."}

{"summary": "As more women work through menopause, European guidelines urge employers to adopt workplace policies that prevent conditions from worsening symptoms, such as cooler temperatures, flexible schedules, reduced stress, bathroom access, and a culture where women feel comfortable disclosing symptoms and requesting accommodations."}

{"summary": "New research from UNC Chapel Hill and SUNY Buffalo suggests women find men who are good storytellers more attractive as long-term partners, possibly because storytelling signals high status. Men did not rate female storytellers as more attractive, though future research is needed to confirm the findings."}

{"summary": "A blog post debunks common meditation myths, arguing meditation suits everyone, has no single correct method, and can boost focus, reduce stress, and help prevent health problems. It introduces a simple one-minute daily morning meditation technique the author learned in China, plus a free guided MP3."}

{"summary": "Robert Schwentke, who directed the Summit action thriller \"Red,\" has been chosen to replace Neil Burger as director of \"Insurgent,\" the sequel to Veronica Roth's \"Divergent\" adaptation. Burger did not return due to the tight production schedule, with Insurgent due in theaters March 20, 2015."}

{"summary": "Prince George's habit of wearing shorts and knee socks traces back to an aristocratic British custom called 'breeching,' which dates to the 16th century and marks when boys switch from dresses to breeches. Etiquette expert William Hanson says the tradition reflects social class and the royal family's values, and that trousers were reserved for men."}

{"summary": "NPR visuals head Brian Boyer and a team received a $35,000 Knight Foundation grant to build Carebot, a prototype tool measuring how much media makes people care, such as completion rates and reader feedback, rather than just page views. The early-stage project aims to launch a prototype by April and favors notification-based updates over dashboards."}

{"summary": "This article argues that every man should own a leather jacket, citing its long association with cool style icons like Brando, Dean, and Beckham, and its versatility with everything from jeans to dress pants. It also offers buying advice on choosing a style, setting a budget, and considering less expensive faux leather options."}

{"summary": "An article claims Bollywood actor Dino Morea has a doppelganger in Scott Foley, who plays Jake in the American TV series Scandal. The piece says the resemblance is striking and notes that others have made the same comparison on Twitter."}

{"summary": "The Sony World Photography Awards has released its shortlist from more than 220,000 entries, with the winner to be announced on 20 April. The article showcases a selection of shortlisted photographs, ranging from Mount Fuji during a marathon to a bullfighting trainee, a grieving Armenian girl, and street scenes across the globe."}

{"summary": "Niantic, the company behind Pokémon Go, plans to bring advertising to the game through sponsored locations, where businesses pay to appear as virtual gym-like spots that draw players to their physical stores. The author jokes that the model is highly effective at driving foot traffic and suggests it could be used for everything from band shows to political rallies."}

{"summary": "A viral post claims a school sent home a permission slip letting parents exempt students from reciting the Pledge of Allegiance, and a parent's response to it is shared online. The article is an opinionated, inflammatory piece blaming Obama and liberals, with no verified details about the school or the slip's actual wording."}

{"summary": "Avik Roy, a Republican health care expert, tells Vox's Matthew Yglesias that the GOP is doomed because conservatism has been driven by white identity politics since Goldwater's 1964 nomination. He argues this blindness paved the way for Donald Trump and says conservatives must build a new, genuinely diverse movement."}

{"summary": "The article argues that marketers often don't know whether their content is actually read, and offers ways to improve readability. It cites Jakob Nielsen's F-pattern eye-tracking research and CoSchedule's heatmap findings that most readers drop off early, plus research showing shares don't correlate with reading. Recommended tactics include the inverted pyramid, scannable text, images, short sentences that pull readers forward, and mobile-friendly design."}

{"summary": "A Connecticut Sacred Heart University student, Nikki Yovino, has been charged with filing a false rape report against two football players in 2016. She later admitted in a police affidavit that she made up the allegation, after which the players, who said the sex was consensual, were cleared. She faces up to five years in prison if convicted."}

{"summary": "Airlines can bump passengers for reasons including overbooking, safety concerns such as aircraft swaps or excess weight, crew transportation needs, and violations of conduct rules. Federal rules require airlines to first ask for volunteers, usually offering vouchers, and involuntarily bumped passengers may receive compensation if delayed more than an hour."}

{"summary": "A flawless 100-carat emerald-cut diamond sold for $22.1 million at Sotheby's New York auction within three minutes of bidding, the most expensive colorless diamond ever auctioned in the city. The winning bidder, who joined by telephone, remained anonymous."}

{"summary": "Former Minneapolis Mayor R.T. Rybak suffered a massive heart attack while cross-country skiing on Saturday, KARE-TV and CBS Minnesota reported. He was in good spirits from the hospital, tweeting poetry about the scare. Rybak had left office just days earlier after 12 years, succeeded by Betsy Hodges."}

{"summary": "Former congressman Tom Perriello unexpectedly entered Virginia's 2017 governor's race, challenging the Democratic establishment's presumed nominee, Lt. Gov. Ralph Northam. The surprise candidacy echoes 2016 presidential dynamics, while Republicans face Ed Gillespie and Corey Stewart in a primary, with both parties' primaries in June."}

{"summary": "An article claims that lying in a 40-degree bath for an hour can burn about 126 calories, comparable to a 20-30 minute brisk walk, and may lower blood sugar via heat shock proteins. It cites a Loughborough University study, though the article's description of that research is loose, and it cautions that baths are no substitute for healthy habits."}

{"summary": "The article argues that cow's milk may harm bones rather than help them. It claims pasteurization destroys enzymes and nutrients that help the body absorb calcium, and it notes that high-dairy countries like the U.S. and EU members have higher osteoporosis rates. These claims are presented without strong scientific support."}

{"summary": "Australian siblings Samuel and Bronte Leighton-Dore plan to have a child for Samuel and his partner Bradley Tennant. Bronte will donate an egg fertilized with Bradley's sperm, and a surrogate will carry the embryo, so both men are genetically linked to the child. The plan is expected within a couple of years."}

{"summary": "Snickle Fritz, a huge dog rescued as a puppy from a cardboard box by a school teacher, is a gentle giant who gets overjoyed whenever Grandma visits. The family lives next door to her, and she gives him belly scratches and kisses, which puts him in paradise."}

{"summary": "Country Fresh recalled about 30,000 cases of precut vegetables, including onions, mushrooms and peppers, sold in nine Southern states after a Georgia product tested positive for Listeria. Listeria naturally lives in soil and water and can spread through soil, manure, and food processing equipment, and no illnesses have been reported so far."}

{"summary": "According to an anonymous source cited by US Weekly, Rob Kardashian and Blac Chyna are expecting a baby girl due in October. The source says Rob is thrilled and Kris Jenner has been offering baby advice. The couple has not yet confirmed the gender publicly."}

{"summary": "Scientists studying Romania's Movile Cave, sealed off for roughly 5.5 million years, have identified 48 species, 33 found nowhere else. The cave's low-oxygen, sulfur-rich air and total darkness support chemosynthetic bacteria, making it one of the few known ecosystems not reliant on sunlight."}

{"summary": "The 89th Academy Awards featured a mix-up in which Faye Dunaway announced La La Land as best picture winner before Moonlight was revealed as the true winner. The ceremony also included Viola Davis's acclaimed speech, Jimmy Kimmel's political jabs at President Trump, and a boycott statement from the director of Best Foreign Language Film winner The Salesman."}

{"summary": "Jarred Walls, an Aboriginal Australian father, overheard two elderly women in a Perth cafe making racist remarks about Aboriginal people. Instead of confronting them angrily, he sent them a pot of tea with a pointed note, then shared the story on Facebook, saying he hoped they would think before speaking again."}

{"summary": "Merriam-Webster sparked social media buzz after tweeting that using \"mad\" to mean \"angry\" is acceptable. When Slate editor Gabriel Roth criticized the dictionary as a \"chill parent,\" Merriam-Webster fired back, \"No one cares how you feel,\" delighting many users. The dictionary's editor said the banter was meant in good fun."}

{"summary": "Salesforce senior VP of global recruiting Ana Recio, who hires over 8,000 people a year, opens interviews by asking candidates their favorite pump-up song and why. The seemingly casual question helps her gauge personality and culture fit, and research suggests strong small talk can give candidates an edge."}

{"summary": "Kelly Clarkson, 31, revealed on The Tonight Show With Jay Leno that she and husband Brandon Blackstock are actively trying to conceive, joking they are trying \"like rabbits.\" She says her stepchildren have made her want a big family, perhaps five kids."}

{"summary": "Data from Eurostat shows nearly 80 per cent of European children were learning a second language in 2014, while UK pupils have only been required to learn languages at primary school since last year. Language education in the UK traditionally began in secondary school, which the article says puts British students at a disadvantage."}

{"summary": "New York artist Hanny Ahern created When I Think About You I Text Myself, a project that lets people send unsent, ill-advised texts to an anonymous number that returns them to the sender at three, six, nine and 12 month intervals. Ahern frames it as a way to reflect on impulsive messages and redirect the urge to text exes or others."}

{"summary": "Lenovo's Yoga Book is a tablet-style computer that replaces the physical keyboard with a touch surface that displays a glowing virtual keyboard and trackpad, using haptic feedback. It also supports Wacom pen writing, can digitize handwritten notes on paper, and has a reversible 10.1-inch main screen."}

{"summary": "The San Antonio Spurs, who went 67-15 but lost in the second round of the playoffs, face uncertainty over whether Tim Duncan (40) or Manu Ginobili (38) will retire. Teammate Danny Green says he doesn't know what to expect, and both players' stats declined this season. Key draft and free agency decisions loom soon."}

{"summary": "Michigan mother Stacey Wehrman Feeley photographed her three-year-old standing on a toilet, thinking it funny, until the girl explained she was practising a preschool lockdown drill for a gun attack. Following the Orlando nightclub shooting that killed 49, Feeley urged politicians to pursue gun control and mental health reforms."}

{"summary": "Yogi Adityanath, a saffron-robed Hindu priest, became chief minister of India's most populous state, Uttar Pradesh, in March and is loved by supporters but criticized for anti-Muslim rhetoric, criminal charges, and controversial policies like anti-Romeo squads and abattoir closures. Analysts question whether he can control his fringe supporters and whether he could become a future BJP leader."}

{"summary": "A suburban Philadelphia military academy, Eastern University, and Cabrini University were placed on lockdown Monday after a student heard what she thought were gunshots. Police found no weapons or injuries, and officials said the sound was likely bubble wrap being popped. The lockdown was lifted about 90 minutes later."}

{"summary": "Michael Easton, fan-favorite actor who played Dr. Silas Clay on General Hospital, is returning to the ABC soap in a brand-new, still-undisclosed role after taping began February 26, 2016, with an airdate set for March 18. Fans had campaigned for his return after Silas was killed off, and producers say the character is new and complex."}

{"summary": "A nine-year study of over 63,000 UK adults found that 'weekend warriors' who squeeze their exercise into one or two days a week had about 30 percent lower risk of dying from any cause than non-exercisers. Even people exercising only one or two days a week without meeting guidelines saw reduced mortality risk."}

{"summary": "This article ranks the 30 highest-paid golfers of all time, mixing current and past players from the PGA Tour and European Tour. Tiger Woods tops the list with $122.5 million in earnings, followed by Phil Mickelson at $94.6 million."}

{"summary": "While surveying white-lipped peccaries in Brazil's Cerrado plateau in 2009, researchers found rare cave drawings of armadillos, birds, reptiles, and big cats. Archaeologists believe hunter-gatherers made the art 4,000 to 10,000 years ago, and conservationists say the find highlights the need to protect these ecosystems."}

{"summary": "This GPS For The Soul guide offers blue-themed scenes and tips to help readers de-stress. It explains that blue is known to promote calm and relaxation, and invites readers to share their own stress-relief methods."}

{"summary": "Marriage therapists across the country argue couples should seek counseling early, before one or both partners disengage. They cite reasons such as preventing hurtful communication patterns, addressing perpetual problems, building resilience before crises, and avoiding worsening resentment. Pre-engagement counseling is also recommended to surface fundamental differences."}

{"summary": "Miles, inspired by a college professor who shared her own mental illness struggles, got a tattoo that reads \"I'm fine\" from most angles but \"save me\" from another. She posted about her depression on Facebook, and the post went viral, making her a voice for people with mental illness."}

{"summary": "This HelloGiggles article offers seven ways to love your body more in 2017 without focusing on changing your appearance. Drawing on wellness coach Annie Robinson, it recommends daily affirmations, shifting focus from diets to how you feel, curating diverse social media, finding enjoyable movement, quitting negative self-talk, and rethinking social media habits."}

{"summary": "Shah Rukh Khan explained why his film Raees was not released alongside Salman Khan's Sultan on Eid: theatre availability for two big films is limited, and Raees still needed some shooting. He said it may now release January 25 or 26, possibly clashing with Hrithik Roshan's Kaabil, which the producers are discussing."}

{"summary": "The article examines how often people should shower, noting conflicting views based on hair and skin type. Dermatologist Stephen Shumack argues showers should be taken only when needed, since daily hot showers can strip natural oils, while virologist John Oxford says showering every other day is harmless if hands and genital areas are washed well."}

{"summary": "Apple has not officially announced it, but sources told BuzzFeed's John Paczkowski that a fall iPhone event will likely take place on Wednesday, September 9, during the week of September 7. The new iPhone is expected to bring a Force Touch display, a better camera, and a faster wireless chip, and new iPads and an Apple TV may also be unveiled."}

{"summary": "A Southern California law firm's report ranks San Bernardino as California's most dangerous city, based on crime, police funding, poverty, unemployment, and other community factors, even though Oakland and Stockton have higher rates of serious violent crime. The report links high poverty across the state to rising living costs and stagnant wages."}

{"summary": "Pornhub's 2013 Porn In Review reports that Americans have the longest average porn-watching sessions in the world, at about 10 minutes 39 seconds, with Mississippi viewers leading among states. The site also logged about 14.8 billion visits worldwide, with January the most popular month and Monday the top day."}

{"summary": "Earworms, the songs that get stuck in your head, are common and usually harmless, but this article offers six science-based tips to get rid of them. Suggestions include avoiding repetitive music, chewing gum, walking at a different tempo, singing another song, managing your mood, socializing with friends, and not trying too hard to suppress them."}

{"summary": "J.K. Rowling revealed on Twitter that Hagrid cannot produce a Patronus, a difficult spell, likely because his hard childhood left him without enough happy memories. Fans responded on social media with sadness for the beloved character."}

{"summary": "In a new American Way interview, 23-year-old Demi Lovato opens up about her battles with bulimia, addiction to alcohol, cocaine and OxyContin, and self-harm. She says she never expected to live to 21, and credits rehab, therapy, and former boyfriend Wilmer Valderrama for her recovery."}

{"summary": "Nine-year-old Molly Sings performed Kasey Chambers' song on The Voice Kids Australia, with lyrics asking whether she is pretty enough and not too broken or outspoken. The emotional performance moved the judges to tears, and Mel B. made a 'Girl Power' pitch for Molly to join her team."}

{"summary": "Britain faces a June 23 referendum on leaving the European Union, with polls showing a near split. Brexit supporters argue it would free business from EU rules and control immigration, while opponents warn of recession, job losses, trade disruption, and possible breakup of the U.K. or the EU."}

{"summary": "The article explains the chalaza, the white, ropey string attached to a raw egg's yolk. It anchors the yolk in the center, is harmless and edible, and its presence signals a fresh egg, since it disappears as the egg ages."}

{"summary": "A Pokemon Go tip claims that finding rare Pokemon is easier in areas with no streets, gyms, or Pokestops nearby and no wild Pokemon spawns. The article notes the theory is unconfirmed but appears to work based on a video's evidence."}

{"summary": "Model Candice Swanepoel has been chosen to wear the Fantasy Bra at the 2013 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show, dubbed the \"Royal Fantasy Bra.\" Created by Mouawad, the $10 million piece has over 4,200 gems, including a 52-carat ruby at the center."}

{"summary": "Blogger Stuart Edge visited the Janice R. Johnson Center for Animals in Deseret, Utah, to walk and play with dogs, then noticed they were sleeping on hard concrete. He and friends bought a carload of dog beds and delivered them to the shelter, brightening the animals' wait for adoption."}

{"summary": "Software company Domo's fourth annual Data Never Sleeps report finds internet activity keeps growing: 3.6 billion people are now online, up from 2.1 billion in 2013, with 18,264,840 megabytes of wireless data used every minute. Tinder gets 972,222 swipes per minute and Giphy serves about 598,217 GIFs."}

{"summary": "An article argues that peeing in the shower could help save water, since skipping the flush on about one of your seven daily wees saves roughly 2,555 litres per year. It notes urine is not toxic and is harmless to skin, though it advises against lingering too long in the shower."}

{"summary": "Analyst Kevin Wang of IHS Technology reports Apple may replace the 16GB base iPhone 7 with a 32GB model, addressing criticism that 16GB is insufficient given storage-heavy features like 4K video and Live Photos. Apple has not confirmed this, and the iPhone 7 is expected in September."}

{"summary": "Katy Perry announced that the official music video for her single \"Roar\" will premiere on September 5, describing it as a \"motion theory adventure\" filmed in \"Junglescope.\" Her new album, \"Prism,\" is scheduled for release on October 22."}

{"summary": "Entertainment site praises iCarly star Jennette McCurdy as a new favorite on Twitter for her sarcastic, relatable humor, highlighting tweets about salads, pajamas, and Hollywood beauty standards. The piece also features funny posts from Anna Kendrick, Lena Dunham, and Sarah Silverman."}

{"summary": "DC Films co-head Geoff Johns confirmed the upcoming team-up movie will be called simply \"Justice League,\" dropping any extra subtitle. Fans welcomed the news as a relief after the convoluted title of Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. The film is set for a November 17, 2017 release, directed by Zack Snyder."}

{"summary": "Apple's jet black iPhone 7 has a high-gloss anodized finish that can show fine micro-abrasions with use, so Apple recommends a case. The article notes that many owners cover their phones anyway, though transparent cases can keep the color visible."}

{"summary": "A reformed sugar addict doctor explains that sugar triggers dopamine in the brain's reward center, creating cravings and crashes that override willpower. He notes added sugar hides in over 70% of packaged foods under many names, and offers tips like avoiding sugary drinks, watching ingredient lists, and sweetening foods yourself to cut back."}

{"summary": "Trey Harris says United barred him from flying with his approved Segway mobility device on his honeymoon trip from Newark to San Diego, despite TSA and United approvals. He was forced to leave the device at the gate, rented a scooter, and later faced a bogus hazmat abandonment message. He shared his account on Medium, seeking an apology and assurance he can bring the device on future flights."}

{"summary": "Michigan Attorney General Bill Schuette argued in a court filing that the state's gay marriage ban is needed to regulate sexual relationships and their procreative capacity, in a case brought by a lesbian couple that goes to trial in Detroit this fall. LGBT advocates called the stance hypocritical and inconsistent with the Supreme Court's DOMA ruling."}

{"summary": "Thomas Blige, father of R&B singer Mary J. Blige, is in critical condition after being stabbed in the neck and elsewhere by an ex-girlfriend during a domestic dispute in Battle Creek, Michigan, early Thursday. Police arrested the woman, who faces arraignment Friday, and the couple had a history of at least seven domestic violence complaints."}

{"summary": "A report, based on unconfirmed sources, claims Avengers: Infinity War will adapt the Infinity Gauntlet comic plot, with Thanos using the gauntlet to impress Death by extinguishing half the universe's life. The Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy, and Nick Fury are expected to appear. Production starts in November for a May 2018 release."}

{"summary": "Michigan mother Stacey Wehrman Feeley shared a photo of her three-year-old standing on a toilet, then broke down when her daughter explained it was a lockdown drill practice for hiding from a gunman at preschool. She has called on politicians to act on gun control."}

{"summary": "Computer science student Jia Li, spotted in Washington Square Park, has naturally long waves that come from an end-only perm about a year ago. She uses Lush shampoo for shine and drinks water mixed with honey and lemon, along with morning fruit, for healthy skin."}

{"summary": "In the MMO Tibia, a Brazilian player named Kharsek became the first to reach level 999 in nearly nine years, unlocking a long-mysterious door. He then passed through quietly and went silent, and the developers won't reveal what lies behind it."}

{"summary": "A four-minute IRS training video parodying NBC's The Apprentice, featuring a fake Donald Trump firing employees who pitch travel-cost cuts, reportedly cost the agency $10,000 to produce in 2011. The IRS says such videos would not be made today, and Rep. Charles Boustany criticized the spending as frivolous."}
{"summary": "Netflix will become the exclusive streaming distributor of "}

{"summary": "California's legislature passed SB 32 and AB 197, reaffirming the state's commitment to fighting climate change by requiring a 40 percent emissions cut below 1990 levels by 2030. The author, from the Union of Concerned Scientists, credits a broad coalition of advocates and public support for the come-from-behind victory over oil industry opposition."}

{"summary": "This Houzz article argues that seven home purchases are worth splurging on, including window coverings, linens, upholstery, room-size rugs, mattresses, original artwork, and countertops. For each, it offers budget-friendly alternatives, such as hemming ready-made curtains, reupholstering secondhand furniture, or choosing emerging artists."}

{"summary": "A teaser trailer for \"Under the Skin\" shows Scarlett Johansson as an alien in human form traveling through Scotland and encountering surreal, nightmarish figures. Directed by Jonathan Glazer, the film debuted at the Telluride Film Festival to strong reviews, though it has no U.S. distribution yet."}

{"summary": "Frontier Developments announced that the Horizons expansion for Elite: Dangerous will launch on Xbox One on June 3 for $30 as an upgrade, bundling the base game with the Planetary Landings and The Engineers expansions. The Engineers arrives on PC May 26 alongside a large free update, and more features like Multicrew and Ship-Launched Fighters are planned for both platforms."}

{"summary": "The article argues Jon Heder fell out of Hollywood's favor after Napoleon Dynamite because he is typecast as that character, his later films flopped, and he pivoted to lucrative voice work and web series. It adds that his clean-living Mormon image gives studios little controversy to exploit, and suggests he could still revive his career if he chooses."}

{"summary": "Saying you're \"busy\" is a common knee-jerk answer at work, but comedian Mindy Kaling and others argue it's a toxic humblebrag that hurts productivity, communication, and energy. Experts suggest rest, deliberate focus, and meaningful time over constant busyness."}

{"summary": "A Cornell veterinary behavior professor explains that cats knock things over mainly to get their owners' attention, often because they're hungry, and to practice their predatory swiping instincts. Deaf cats are more likely to do it since they aren't startled by the noise."}

{"summary": "Career coach Tina Nicolai, who has reviewed over 40,000 résumés, says the three most annoying flaws are overly long summaries, overused jargon like \"team player\" and \"out-of-the-box,\" and an overly formal, rigid tone. She recommends short achievement bullets, specific language, and a personality that engages the reader."}

{"summary": "Bloomberg named Singapore the best-value city for foreign business after a Savills report found it offers the best property-rental value among 10 major global hubs. Singapore scored lowest (best) at 16.1, while Mumbai scored worst at 74.7, based on setup costs relative to per-capita GDP."}

{"summary": "This article ranks the world's ten most valuable brands as of May 22, 2020, with Apple first at an estimated $205.5 billion, followed by Google at $167.7 billion and Microsoft third. Amazon, Facebook, Coca-Cola, Samsung, Disney, Toyota, and McDonald's round out the list, which the article distinguishes from rankings by company market capitalization."}

{"summary": "Oxfam's new food index ranks the Netherlands first for plentiful, nutritious, affordable food, ahead of France and Switzerland, while the US and Japan fall outside the top 20 due to obesity and diabetes. Chad ranks last among 125 nations."}

{"summary": "Politico reported Hillary Clinton's pneumonia is not severe but that chronic dehydration, worsened by her reluctance to drink water, has caused tension with her staff. The article mocks the contrast with her 2008 claim that she drinks "}

{"summary": "HBO's Game of Thrones season seven will be delayed past its usual April debut, with showrunners David Benioff and Dan Weiss saying they pushed filming later to capture grim, gray winter weather that matches the story's tone."}

{"summary": "A man named Charlie received a call from a scammer claiming he owed the IRS over $3,000 and faced property seizure unless he paid by credit card. Instead of complying, Charlie turned the call into a faith-based conversation, referring the caller to his \"Father\" El Shaddai, and ended up getting the scammer to pray the Sinner's Prayer."}

{"summary": "YouTubers GismoSlip froze a Samsung Galaxy Note 7 in a block of ice and dropped it from up to 100 feet. The phone survived more than 23 hours submerged and frozen without a scratch and stayed fully functional, though the article notes its software has been bricking for some owners."}

{"summary": "Google's preliminary Black Friday 2013 data showed Ugg boots were the top trending fashion item among shoppers, ranking fourth overall behind video game consoles, tablets, and Minecraft Legos. The article notes Uggs remain popular despite falling out of trendy favor, with over a quarter of American women surveyed owning a pair."}

{"summary": "Northwestern's Medill School of Journalism plans to shut down its widely used alumni email list on May 30, replacing it with the new OurNorthwestern social network. Many alumni are angry, arguing the change fixes nothing broken, and some have already set up an alternative Google Group."}

{"summary": "Apple unveiled a 12.9-inch iPad Pro at its iPhone 6s event, rivaling Microsoft's Surface. Surprisingly, Apple brought Microsoft employees on stage to demonstrate Microsoft Office running on the device, drawing gasps from the crowd."}

{"summary": "Samantha Mawdsley, a 30-year-old from Manchester, received an unsolicited penis photo from a man on a dating site after reviewing a restaurant. She responded by sending him penis images and posting the exchange on Facebook with mocking stickers, and the post has been widely shared, with many women and men praising her."}

{"summary": "Two unidentified Western tourists were paraded around Gili Trawangan, Indonesia, with signs admitting theft, in a long-running local practice used because police have no permanent presence on the islands. Locals say it keeps crime low, but critics note the accused have no clear legal process or chance to defend themselves."}

{"summary": "In a Super Soul Sunday interview, Oprah Winfrey asks Maya Angelou about prayer, inner peace, and what she knows for sure. Angelou says prayer changes things for both the person prayed for and herself, that she finds peace by centering herself, and that love saves us all."}

{"summary": "The article presents surprising facts about Mary Shelley, author of Frankenstein, covering her intellectual family, her early elopement with poet Percy Bysshe Shelley, the rumors surrounding Harriet Westbrook's death, the dream and ghost-story challenge that inspired her novel, and the many personal tragedies she endured, including losing three children."}

{"summary": "Julie Andrews has given her blessing to Emily Blunt taking over the role of Mary Poppins in Mary Poppins Returns, according to director Rob Marshall's report to Blunt. Blunt said the approval eased her nerves. The sequel draws more from the original books than the 1964 film, giving Blunt room to create her own version of the character."}

{"summary": "Cornell University's Board of Trustees approved Elizabeth Garrett, provost at the University of Southern California, as the school's first female president, succeeding David Skorton, who is leaving to lead the Smithsonian. Garrett takes office July 1, 2015, as Cornell turns 150 and expands into New York City."}

{"summary": "Pete's Dragon director David Lowery says Disney contracts bar three things from its films: beheadings, impalement, and smoking. The article notes these rules have changed over time, citing Pinocchio's cigar scene and Ursula's impalement in The Little Mermaid, and that a 2015 Variety report said Disney banned smoking in G, PG, and PG-13 films unless historically pertinent."}
